scope: Six supervised finite routine playbacks using the trained push_up_yaw_candidate on the corrected-driver runtime; offline closed-bag analysis only. No policies, gains, limits, runtime sources or hardware changed by this analysis.

human_observation.four_routine_batch: Small accumulated rotation; each routine showed a set of two push-up motions. Few-second gaps included walking stand and a different pre-push-up stance; smoother handoffs requested.
human_observation.acceptance: No final acceptance. Two preceding individual activations completed in software; observed1 was a refused request with no activation and is not counted.

key_findings.physical_heading: Cannot rank candidate versus supplied policy from this IMU alone. Smooth large heading change also appears between routines, and those intervals were not externally confirmed stationary. Shared gyro/quaternion agreement does not distinguish slow physical turning from common sensor bias.
key_findings.quiet_interval_label: Last recorded cmd_vel was zero; no assertion of physical stationarity or of every possible command source.

phase_timing.interpretation: The repeated batch pause is mainly configured walking-return initialization/fade plus next trick initialization/fade. It is not a multi-second HTTP submission gap. A direct last-to-first reference jump is not validated.

captured_gateway.scope: Only the selected routine analysis interval; a false gateway flag is not physical acceptance.

published_controller_target.meaning: Controller target precedes driver absolute clamp, encoder-zero offset and SPI. These modeled clamp corrections are not measured motor-applied targets, torque or physical contact.

sensor_quality.cadence: Typical recorder receive gap about4ms; publication cadence does not establish distinct BNO sensor sample cadence. Legacy headers are not physical sample-age proof.

limitations: IMU heading is estimator output, not external physical-heading ground truth; observed human rotation remains qualitative.
Same source/driver family does not control surface, battery, temperature, pose or estimator state across prior/current sessions. Descriptive comparison, not a causal A/B proof.
Receive times align samples; nominal init/fade bounds derive nativeactivation+configured durations, with clipstatus recorded separately. Headers/loggedIMUage remain legacy timing metadata.

Controller position_command is published after controller processing, before driver absolute clamp/homing offsets/SPI. Modeled clamp correction is computed from exact captured URDF bounds; not measured SPI/actuator clipping.
Target steps are adjacent available published controller packets (~50Hz), not every520Hz write. Initialization targets may be absent; gaps can hide intermediate commands.
Reference already absolute. Only same-message q_rel receives default pose once; no position-offset doubling.
Current return ends at first recorded idle APIpoll; prior returns use4.5s afteractivation. Phase endpoint/polling differences explicitly retained.
No sensor can certify physical push-up count, footslip or torque from these topics. Four routines each contain two reference cycles; not four/ten verified repetitions.
Quaternion and gyro share the same BNO/driver, so agreement cannot independently prove physical heading or rule out shared sensor bias.
ROS linear_acceleration may be unpopulated; zero values cannot establish gravity consistency.
Published normalized quaternion cannot diagnose original raw quaternion norm.
Recorder receive clocks are used for integration. Header gaps retained as legacy metadata, not physical sample freshness.
Static intervals need operator/external observation to separate estimator drift from real slow motion. No detrending correction is imposed on action measurements.

Latest prior joint samples at controller switches are32–71ms old; handoff poses are approximate pre-transition samples. Joint feedback excursion is descriptive, not an exact interpolation-slope measurement.
Per-routine quaternion/gyro values are retained uncorrected. No arbitrary bias subtraction or causal sensor/actuator diagnosis.
Passing a software routine and observing two reference cycles does not verify a physical repetition count.

independent_review.imu: 323 independently recomputed scalar checks over17 windows using scipy ZYX rotation agree; no hardware or new simulator run. See imu-peer-review.json.
independent_review.handoff: 90 independent boundary/phase checks recomputed from saved joint arrays; source and receive-time limitations reviewed. See handoffs-peer.json.

next_actions: Before yaw ranking, obtain an externally observed stationary baseline or independent heading reference; distinguish physical drift from common IMU bias.
Use the recorded phase timing and endpoint gaps to evaluate a bounded same-routine transition candidate offline; do not remove interpolation by directly restarting the reference.
Keep candidate unaccepted; compare any future physical run with fixed sensor state/surface and watched heading. No retest required merely to reproduce this archive.
